name: lex-runtime
description: Amazon Lex provides both build and runtime endpoints. Each endpoint provides a set of operations (API).

subcommands.name: delete-session
subcommands.description: Removes session information for a specified bot, alias, and user ID

options.name: --bot-name
options.description: The name of the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --bot-alias
options.description: The alias in use for the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --user-id
options.description: The identifier of the user associated with the session data

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: get-session
subcommands.description: Returns session information for a specified bot, alias, and user ID

options.name: --bot-name
options.description: The name of the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --bot-alias
options.description: The alias in use for the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --user-id
options.description: The ID of the client application user. Amazon Lex uses this to identify a user's conversation with your bot

options.name: --checkpoint-label-filter
options.description: A string used to filter the intents returned in the recentIntentSummaryView structure.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: post-content
subcommands.description: Sends user input (text or speech) to Amazon Lex. Clients use this API to send text and audio requests to Amazon Lex at runtime.

options.name: --bot-name
options.description: Name of the Amazon Lex bot

options.name: --bot-alias
options.description: Alias of the Amazon Lex bot

options.name: --user-id
options.description: The ID of the client application user. Amazon Lex uses this to identify a user's conversation with your bot.

options.name: --session-attributes
options.description: You pass this value as the x-amz-lex-session-attributes HTTP header. Application-specific information passed between Amazon Lex and a client application.

options.name: --request-attributes
options.description: You pass this value as the x-amz-lex-request-attributes HTTP header. Request-specific information passed between Amazon Lex and a client application.

options.name: --content-type
options.description: You pass this value as the Content-Type HTTP header.   Indicates the audio format or text.

options.name: --accept
options.description: You pass this value as the Accept HTTP header.

options.name: --input-stream
options.description: User input in PCM or Opus audio format or text format as described in the Content-Type HTTP header.

options.name: --active-contexts
options.description: A list of contexts active for the request.

options.name: outfile
options.description: Filename where the content will be saved

subcommands.name: post-text
subcommands.description: Sends user input to Amazon Lex. Client applications can use this API to send requests to Amazon Lex at runtime.

options.name: --bot-name
options.description: The name of the Amazon Lex bot

options.name: --bot-alias
options.description: The alias of the Amazon Lex bot

options.name: --user-id
options.description: The ID of the client application user. Amazon Lex uses this to identify a user's conversation with your bot.

options.name: --session-attributes
options.description: Application-specific information passed between Amazon Lex and a client application. For more information, see Setting Session Attributes

options.name: --request-attributes
options.description: Request-specific information passed between Amazon Lex and a client application. The namespace x-amz-lex: is reserved for special attributes.

options.name: --input-text
options.description: The text that the user entered (Amazon Lex interprets this text)

options.name: --active-contexts
options.description: A list of contexts active for the request.

options.name: --cli-input-json
options.description: Performs service operation based on the JSON string provided. The JSON string follows the format provided by ``--generate-cli-skeleton``.

options.name: --generate-cli-skeleton
options.description: Prints a JSON skeleton to standard output without sending an API request.

subcommands.name: put-session
subcommands.description: Creates a new session or modifies an existing session with an Amazon Lex bot. Use this operation to enable your application to set the state of the bot.

options.name: --bot-name
options.description: The name of the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --bot-alias
options.description: The alias in use for the bot that contains the session data

options.name: --user-id
options.description: The ID of the client application user. Amazon Lex uses this to identify a user's conversation with your bot

options.name: --session-attributes
options.description: Map of key/value pairs representing the session-specific context information.

options.name: --dialog-action
options.description: Sets the next action that the bot should take to fulfill the conversation

options.name: --recent-intent-summary-view
options.description: A summary of the recent intents for the bot. You can use the intent summary view to set a checkpoint label on an intent and modify attributes of intents.

options.name: --accept
options.description: The message that Amazon Lex returns in the response can be either text or speech based depending on the value of this field.

options.name: --active-contexts
options.description: A list of contexts active for the request.

options.name: outfile
options.description: Filename where the content will be saved
